integrity: The proof reduces each transition to x^2 congruent to y modulo b-1. For prime b-1, composing the two transitions forces exact order three, leaving only the two nontrivial cube roots of unity. An exact quotient-and-remainder criterion then gives the stated quadratic inequality. The attached finite checker independently compares direct dynamics with the theorem for every prime below 20000.
scientific_limitations: The theorem classifies only nontrivial period-two orbits whose two states are positive one-digit states, under the assumption that b-1 is prime. Composite b-1 and cycles containing larger states are outside scope. Targeted searches found no equivalent prime-modulus theorem, but unindexed recreational literature remains a residual originality risk.
title: Prime-modulus rigidity for one-digit Kaprekar two-cycles
